about: Public facts about payers and codes for owner rule 4.2 (codes a payer almost never pays). One entry per payer group and code: the verdict (note, claim, never_payable, unclear), the payer's published rule, what the note or claim must show, and the sources with the exact sentence quoted. Every source was fetched twice on 2026-11-26 and its title, date and quotes matched both times. No counts, dollars or practice data: the evidence from the store is computed live by the application. applies_when names a condition the application checks on the item's own claim before it shows the entry's verdict: em_with_modifier_25 (an office or outpatient E/M line of the same claim and date carries modifier 25). When the condition does not hold, or cannot be checked, the item shows the rule with the verdict unclear.

verdicts.note: fixable by what the visit note shows
verdicts.claim: fixable on the claim (modifier, code, diagnosis order, provider enrollment, a separate claim, the right payer)
verdicts.never_payable: not payable under the cited rule; the item stays pursued until the owner accepts the pattern
verdicts.unclear: no published rule found that explains the denial

rules.rule: UnitedHealthcare required prior authorization for G6001 (image-guided radiation therapy, IGRT) until 12/31/2025 in its Medicare Advantage, commercial, Community Plan and Individual Exchange plans; G6001 is a termed code from 2026. Its Medicare Advantage policy finds no Medicare NCD or LCD for IGRT and applies the commercial medical policy 'Radiation Therapy: Fractionation, Image-Guidance, and Special Services', whose versions before 03/01/2026 said IGRT is not medically necessary for superficial treatment of skin cancer, including superficial radiation therapy or electronic brachytherapy, when the policy's listed criteria are not met. For a service date before 2026, G6001 was paid only with an approved authorization that listed it, and only when those criteria were met: a denial for no authorization (CO-197) is fixed on the claim when an authorization listed G6001, and a denial for coverage guidelines (CO-272) only by a note that shows the listed criteria were met. The earlier versions themselves could not be fetched: the revision note is the payer's own record of what they said. From 2026 ultrasound guidance for surface radiation therapy is CPT 77439, once per course, reported with 77437 or 77438.
rules.what_to_show: Check whether an approved UnitedHealthcare authorization for the course listed G6001; if one did, resubmit with that authorization number. With no such authorization, a denial for no authorization (CO-197) stands. A denial for coverage guidelines (CO-272) is appealed only with a note that shows the policy's listed criteria for image guidance were met. For 2026 dates, report 77439 (never G6001), once per course, with 77437 or 77438, and include it in the authorization request.

rules.rule: CPT 2026 (effective 01/01/2026) says not to report the surface radiation therapy codes 77436, 77437, 77438 and 77439 together with hyperthermia 77600, and 77401 was deleted in favor of those codes. Hyperthermia given in the same course as surface radiation therapy is therefore not separately reportable for 2026 service dates, and a payer that edits by CPT instructions treats it as included in the radiation service. Medicare's national coverage of local hyperthermia with radiation for superficial skin malignancies (NCD 110.1) is a coverage rule and does not change the CPT coding instruction.
rules.what_to_show: No note changes this for a course of surface radiation therapy (77436-77439). Do not use modifier 59 or XS to get around a CPT 'do not report' instruction. 77600 can be reported only with a radiation service outside 77436-77439, and the note must name that service and its date.

sources.quote: (77401 has been deleted. For surface radiation therapy, see 77436, 77437, 77438, 77439)

Local hyperthermia is covered under Medicare when used in connection with radiation therapy for the treatment of primary or metastatic cutaneous or subcutaneous superficial malignancies. It is not covered when used alone or in connection with chemotherapy.

by_service_date.rule: When the plan is VA community care, VA pays only for services within the authorized referral: services outside its scope need VA approval before care is given (the Request for Service process), and claims are processed with CMS's NCCI and MUE edits. Medicare's NCD 110.1 covers local hyperthermia with radiation for superficial skin malignancies, so the question is the referral's scope, not coverage.
by_service_date.what_to_show: Check the referral (its standardized episode of care) for hyperthermia. If the referral or an approved Request for Service covered 77600 on that date, resubmit or appeal with the referral number and the approval. If not, it cannot be fixed after the fact; for future courses ask VA for approval before care (and, from 2026, do not report 77600 with 77436-77439 at all).

by_service_date.rule: State Medicaid pays only for services of enrolled providers. 42 CFR 455.410(b) makes the state require every ordering or referring physician or other professional providing services under the State plan to be enrolled, and 455.410(d) lets a Medicare-enrolled provider enroll so Medicaid can process the Medicare cost-sharing (crossover) claims. The remark codes N767 (provider not enrolled in the member's state Medicaid), N570 (credentialing data), N198 (rendering provider not affiliated with the pay-to provider), N288 and N255 (rendering and billing taxonomy) and reason B7 (provider not certified or eligible for this service on this date) name an enrollment problem, not a problem with the code. Reasons 24 and 109 mean the member's managed care plan, not fee-for-service Medicaid, must be billed.
by_service_date.what_to_show: Fix the claim, not the note: confirm the rendering provider is enrolled with the member's state Medicaid and linked to the billing group, put the rendering and billing taxonomy codes on the claim, and resubmit within the filing limit. When the remittance says 24 or 109, send the claim to the member's Medicaid managed care plan. When it says 22, bill the primary payer first and send its remittance with the claim.

rules.rule: Anthem's commercial reimbursement policy 'Bundled Services and Supplies - Professional' (C-08003) lists G2211 in Section 1, services and supplies not eligible for separate reimbursement, and says modifiers do not override that denial. Checked on the Virginia plan's copy of the policy and its Section 1 coding grid; the Kentucky copy was not found online, so confirm it with Anthem Kentucky.
rules.what_to_show: No note changes this. Stop reporting G2211 to Anthem commercial plans unless the contract says Anthem pays it; ask Anthem Kentucky for its own C-08003 Section 1 list to confirm.

sources.quote: The health plan considers certain services and supplies to be ineligible for separate reimbursement when reported by a professional provider, unless provider, state, or federal contracts and/or requirements indicate otherwise.
In addition, modifiers will not override the denial for the always bundled services and/or supplies listed in the embedded document.
G2211 Visit complexity inherent to evaluation and management associated with medical care services that serve as the continuing focal point for all needed health care services
Services considered always bundled will not be allowed for separate reimbursement when billed by a professional provider.

rules.what_to_show: No note changes this. Stop reporting G2211 to UnitedHealthcare commercial and Individual Exchange plans.

A: No, visit complexity for services G2211 and G0545 are structured in the reimbursement for evaluation and management services and not paid separately.

rules.rule: Medicare does not pay G2211 when the office or outpatient E/M visit it is added to is reported with modifier 25, except, from 01/01/2025, when the service that required modifier 25 is an allowed Part B preventive service, an immunization administration or an annual wellness visit. A minor procedure on the same day (for example a destruction or a biopsy) is not such a service, so G2211 on that visit is not payable. Medicare Advantage plans that follow Medicare apply the same edit. A G2211 line also fails when its E/M line is not paid (reason B15, remark N122).
rules.what_to_show: No note changes this when the E/M carries modifier 25 for a procedure. Report G2211 only on an E/M without modifier 25, or with modifier 25 only for an allowed preventive service, immunization or annual wellness visit. When the E/M itself was denied, work the E/M first; G2211 follows it.

rules.rule: Medicare does not cover routine foot care, which includes trimming, cutting, clipping or debriding nails, except in the presence of a systemic condition with class findings (one Class A finding, two Class B findings, or one Class B and two Class C findings) or for mycotic nails with pain, secondary infection or marked limitation of ambulation. The Medicare Administrative Contractors' billing articles require modifier Q7, Q8 or Q9 on claims based on a systemic condition. A Medicare Advantage plan covers what Medicare covers.
rules.what_to_show: The note must name the systemic condition and the class findings found on that day (or the mycotic nail findings with pain, infection or limited walking), and, for conditions that need it, the doctor of medicine or osteopathy actively managing it and the date the patient was last seen. The claim must carry Q7, Q8 or Q9 matching the class findings, with the systemic condition's diagnosis.
